SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #2
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Where does the sun rise? (1 mark)
   A. In the north
   B. In the east
   C. In the south
   D. In the west

2. Why are cardinal points better than left and right for giving directions? (1 mark)
   A. They only work at night
   B. They are shorter to say
   C. They are used only by pilots
   D. They do not change when you turn around

3. Where does the sun set? (1 mark)
   A. In the east
   B. In the north
   C. In the south
   D. In the west

4. What do we call describing where a county is by naming the places around it? (1 mark)
   A. Scale
   B. Relative location
   C. Population
   D. Rainfall

5. Which county borders Uganda? (1 mark)
   A. Kitui
   B. Nairobi
   C. Nyeri
   D. Busia

6. County X covers 8 grid squares and County Y covers 5 grid squares. Which statement is correct? (1 mark)
   A. We cannot compare them
   B. They are the same size
   C. County X is bigger than County Y
   D. County Y is bigger than County X

7. Which country lies to the south of Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Ethiopia
   B. Tanzania
   C. Uganda
   D. South Sudan

8. What would you draw as a symbol for a river on a map? (1 mark)
   A. A black circle
   B. A red square
   C. A green triangle
   D. A wavy blue line

9. What is a valley? (1 mark)
   A. Low land between hills or mountains
   B. A big lake
   C. A very high peak
   D. A huge flat plain

10. What is the difference between a museum and a cultural centre? (1 mark)
   A. A cultural centre has no dances
   B. A museum mainly keeps objects, a cultural centre shows living culture
   C. A museum is always outdoors
   D. There is no difference

11. Which monument in Nairobi remembers Kenya's independence in 1963? (1 mark)
   A. Thimlich Ohinga
   B. Uhuru Gardens
   C. Fort Jesus
   D. Lamu Fort

12. What is a historic built environment? (1 mark)
   A. A new shopping mall
   B. A natural forest
   C. A place built long ago that tells us about the past
   D. A river

13. In a chart of who gives and who needs, what does a farmer give? (1 mark)
   A. Food
   B. Learning
   C. Health care
   D. Transport

14. Who brings medicine and equipment to hospitals? (1 mark)
   A. Only farmers
   B. Drivers and traders
   C. Nobody
   D. Only teachers

15. What is trade? (1 mark)
   A. Playing games
   B. Growing crops only
   C. Buying and selling goods
   D. Building houses

16. What is one benefit of interdependence? (1 mark)
   A. We get goods and services we cannot make ourselves
   B. We stop trading
   C. We stop working
   D. We become poor

17. Why do many people live near rivers and lakes? (1 mark)
   A. Rivers are always dry
   B. Lakes have no fish
   C. Water is available for drinking and farming
   D. Rivers are dangerous

18. What do we call an area where many people live close together? (1 mark)
   A. Wild
   B. Densely populated
   C. Empty
   D. Sparsely populated

19. Which artefacts are carved at Kisii and sold to visitors? (1 mark)
   A. Plastic toys
   B. Soapstone carvings
   C. Iron bridges
   D. Glass windows

20. Which is a ceremony? (1 mark)
   A. A road
   B. A wedding
   C. A market
   D. A rainy day

21. Which of these is an aspect of traditional culture? (1 mark)
   A. Traditional food
   B. Mountains
   C. Rivers
   D. Rainfall

22. Why do we recite the school motto? (1 mark)
   A. To waste time
   B. To hide
   C. To remember what the school stands for
   D. To scare others

23. Which is NOT allowed in Kenyan schools? (1 mark)
   A. Talking to pupils
   B. Guiding and counselling pupils
   C. Beating pupils
   D. Praising pupils

24. Which of these is a natural resource? (1 mark)
   A. A road
   B. A tractor
   C. Water in a river
   D. A school building

25. What is a citizen? (1 mark)
   A. A member of a country or community with rights and duties
   B. A kind of law
   C. A type of school
   D. A visitor who never returns

26. Which behaviour shows patriotism? (1 mark)
   A. Laughing during the anthem
   B. Damaging public property
   C. Standing respectfully during the national anthem
   D. Ignoring the flag

27. What is a duty? (1 mark)
   A. Something you are expected to do
   B. Something you may not do
   C. A gift
   D. A game

28. What does Stop-Think-Share teach? (1 mark)
   A. Think before you post
   B. Share your password
   C. Ignore rules
   D. Post quickly

29. Where does a county government get money? (1 mark)
   A. From the national government and local fees and taxes
   B. From nowhere
   C. Only from fines
   D. Only from gifts

30. Which best describes the difference between the governor and an MCA? (1 mark)
   A. The governor runs the county; an MCA makes laws and checks the governor
   B. An MCA is above the governor
   C. They do the same job
   D. The governor makes laws

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Give two ways in which Mount Kenya is useful. (2 marks)

32. Explain how you can find east in the morning without a compass. (2 marks)

33. State three duties of a village elder. (3 marks)

34. Explain how a cultural centre is different from a museum. (3 marks)

35. Describe four things a school can do to promote child rights. (4 marks)

36. Give three benefits of industries to a county. (3 marks)

37. Explain how a farmer and a trader depend on each other. (3 marks)

38. Write a short poem of four lines about the benefits of industries in your county. (5 marks)

39. Name two historic places in Kenya and the town or county where each is found. (2 marks)

40. Explain what would happen in a community if farmers stopped growing food. (4 marks)

41. Why do people trade? (2 marks)

42. Name the four in-between points on a compass and say between which cardinal points each lies. (4 marks)

43. Describe how health workers, farmers and teachers depend on each other. (4 marks)

44. Name two places where you can find information about your school's history. (2 marks)

45. Write a peace message and explain how it can help other pupils. (4 marks)

46. Using time words, write a short history of a school that opened in 1985 and built a library in 2000. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #2 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — In the east
   The sun rises in the east and sets in the west.

2. D — They do not change when you turn around
   Left and right change with the way you face, but north, east, south and west stay the same.

3. D — In the west
   The sun sets in the west.

4. B — Relative location
   Relative location compares a place with its neighbours.

5. D — Busia
   Busia is on the border with Uganda.

6. C — County X is bigger than County Y
   8 squares is more land than 5 squares.

7. B — Tanzania
   Tanzania borders Kenya to the south.

8. D — A wavy blue line
   Rivers are shown as wavy blue lines.

9. A — Low land between hills or mountains
   A valley is a low area between higher land.

10. B — A museum mainly keeps objects, a cultural centre shows living culture
   Cultural centres let visitors see and take part in living culture.

11. B — Uhuru Gardens
   Uhuru Gardens is where the Kenyan flag was first raised at independence.

12. C — A place built long ago that tells us about the past
   Historic built places are old places made by people.

13. A — Food
   Farmers give food to the community.

14. B — Drivers and traders
   Transport workers carry goods to hospitals.

15. C — Buying and selling goods
   Trade is buying and selling.

16. A — We get goods and services we cannot make ourselves
   Sharing skills gives us more goods and services.

17. C — Water is available for drinking and farming
   Water is a basic need.

18. B — Densely populated
   Dense means crowded.

19. B — Soapstone carvings
   Kisii is known for soapstone carving.

20. B — A wedding
   A wedding is a special event with customs.

21. A — Traditional food
   Dressing, food, housing, artefacts, games and ceremonies are aspects of culture.

22. C — To remember what the school stands for
   Reciting reminds us of the school's aims.

23. C — Beating pupils
   Teachers are not allowed to beat pupils.

24. C — Water in a river
   Water in a river is from nature.

25. A — A member of a country or community with rights and duties
   Citizens belong to a community and have rights and duties.

26. C — Standing respectfully during the national anthem
   Respecting national symbols shows love for the country.

27. A — Something you are expected to do
   A duty is a responsibility.

28. A — Think before you post
   We should think about whether it is true, kind and safe.

29. A — From the national government and local fees and taxes
   Counties get shared money and collect local fees.

30. A — The governor runs the county; an MCA makes laws and checks the governor
   They have different roles.

SECTION B
----
31. (2 marks)
   Answer: It gives water for rivers and it attracts tourists. Accept rich soils for farming.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct use.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: Face the direction where the sun rises. That direction is east.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for using the rising sun, 1 mark for naming east.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Welcome visitors, settle small quarrels and call meetings. Accept reporting problems.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each duty.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: A museum mainly keeps and shows objects. A cultural centre lets people see and join in living culture such as dances and crafts. Some places do both.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each description and 1 mark for the difference.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: Make posters, sing songs on child protection, set up a suggestion box, and include all children in activities.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each activity.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: They give jobs, they buy farmers' produce, and they pay taxes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each benefit.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: The farmer grows crops and sells them to the trader. The trader carries the crops to town and sells them. The trader needs the crops and the farmer needs the buyer.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

38. (5 marks)
   Answer: A poem that mentions jobs, income and goods, is neat and rhymes or has rhythm.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for four lines, 1 mark for jobs, 1 mark for income or goods, 1 mark for a title, 1 mark for correct language.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: Fort Jesus in Mombasa and Thimlich Ohinga in Migori County. Accept Lamu Old Town or Gede Ruins.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct place with its location.

40. (4 marks)
   Answer: There would be a shortage of food. Traders would have nothing to sell. Prices would go up. People could become hungry and ill.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each consequence.

41. (2 marks)
   Answer: People trade to get the goods they need but cannot make, and to earn money from the goods they produce.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: North-east (between north and east), south-east (between south and east), south-west (between south and west), north-west (between north and west).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct in-between point with its place.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Health workers keep farmers and teachers well. Farmers give food to health workers and teachers. Teachers teach the children of farmers and health workers. Each group needs the others to live well.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct link.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: The headteacher or teachers, and the school records or log book. Accept old photographs or elders.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each source.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: Talk, do not fight. It reminds pupils to solve problems with words, so there are fewer fights and everyone feels safe.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a clear message, 1 mark for correct language, 2 marks for the explanation.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: The school was opened in 1985. Later, in 2000, a library was built. Today, pupils read books in the library.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dates, 1 mark for order, 1 mark for time words.
